‘No. Only for yourself.

And Chade can see to the King’s needs.’
‘Chade.
The name is almost familiar, as if I heard it before, long ago.’
‘He is supposed to have died, long ago.
Before that, he was seen about the keep.’
‘To live all these years as a shadow,’ he marvelled.
‘And he plans to go on living as a shadow.’
‘You need not fear I’ll betray him.’
Burrich sounded hurt.
‘I know.
I am just so …’
‘I know.
Go on, then.
You’ve told me enough for me to do my part.
I’ll be there with the horses and supplies.
What time?’
‘Sometime in the night, when the feasting is still lively.
I don’t know.
I’ll get word to you somehow.’
He shrugged.
‘As soon as it gets dark, I’ll go out there and wait.’
‘Burrich.
Thank you.’
‘He is my king.
She is my queen.
I need no thanks from you to do my duty.’
I left Burrich and crept down his staircase.
I kept to the shadows and extended every sense I had to try to be sure no one was spying on me.

Nighteyes came panting to meet me.

I hugged him hard.
Foolishness, he told me gruffly.
Go on, now.

My thanks.
My brother.

Excitement thundered through me.
I would know no real rest until all had been accomplished.

I brought with me a number of scrolls on herbs.
Kettricken was reclining on a couch before the hearth, and I could see that her fall had caused her more pain in truth than she cared to admit.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: I left Burrich and crept down his staircase. I kept to the shadows and extended every sense I had to try to be sure no one was spying on me. paragraphPairs.sourceText: At mid-morning I was admitted to the Queen’s chamber. I brought with me a number of scrolls on herbs. Kettricken was reclining on a couch before the hearth, and I could see that her fall had caused her more pain in truth than she cared to admit. She looked little better than she had the night before, but I greeted her warmly, and proceeded to work my way through every herb listed, one after the other, with much discussion as to the benefits of each. I succeeded in boring most of her ladies away, and she finally dismissed the last three to bring tea, find her more pillows, and look for another scroll on herbs that Kettricken said was in Verity’s study. Little Rosemary had long since dozed off in a warm corner by the hearth. As soon as the rustle of their skirts had faded, I spoke quickly, knowing I had little time.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: В середине утра меня впустили в покои королевы. Я принёс с собой несколько свитков о травах. Кетриккен полулежала на кушетке перед очагом, и я видел, что падение причинило ей куда больше боли, чем она желала признать. Выглядела она немногим лучше, чем накануне вечером, но я тепло поприветствовал её и принялся разбирать одну за другой все перечисленные травы, подробно обсуждая пользу каждой. Мне удалось наскучить большей части её придворных дам, и наконец она отослала последних троих принести чаю, найти ей ещё подушек и разыскать другой свиток о травах, который, по словам Кетриккен, лежал в кабинете Верити. Маленькая Розмари уже давно задремала в тёплом уголке у очага. Как только шелест их юбок затих, я быстро заговорил, зная, что времени у меня мало.
